summary: Human skin, type IV on the Fitzpatrick scale, a second person of the tone (structure 2), with light scattering under the surface and fine pores.
_comment: STRUCTURE 2 of the tone (Phase23 23.3, RD-P23-4): Skin_FitzpatrickIV_Clean_Base_s001_v01 with its own skin map, the maker's Skin2 (more weathered: a stronger tan on the face and hands, coarser mottling, few flecks, little flush; gen_synth_skin.STRUCTURES), the same person at every tone. The Material token carries the structure and the Variant the tone, so lips and nails pair as before; one Lips_FitzpatrickIV serves every structure (RD-P23-5: the maps agree inside the lips' zone). FITTED (Phase21, RD-P21-1): the article carries its tone AND its skin map, drawn for MakeHuman_Body_v01 (hm08; RD-SKM-1), as its own base_color_map. The map is the tone's colour picture stored as a multiplier (brightest ~1) and base_color_const is the tone raised by the same factor, so the skin renders its measured tone on average (RD-P21-3; tools/converters/fit/gen_skin_maps.py). The scatter colour follows the base, the picture and the Creator's tint included (RD-P21-4). On another mesh, a binding that supplies a white picture gives the tone alone (the Carrier rule). The pores still tile at 1 cm through the placement (s001); the map samples the mesh's own UVs. Before Phase21: Human skin, Fitzpatrick type IV (Phase07 step 7.3). SUBSURFACE: skin's look is light scattering inside it. Topology-free (CM2): a tone plus a tiling micro-surface at real size, so it works on any mesh. Values from Physically Based `Skin IV` (albedo, IOR 1.4, roughness 0.5, scatter distance). `subsurface_radius` is in metres (OpenPBR scene units; Learnings/MaterialX M4): Physically Based gives the diffuse mean free path in cm (0.367, 0.137, 0.068), so 3.67 mm red, with the channels over it as the scale. `subsurface_weight` 1.0 and `subsurface_color` = the albedo (judgement): skin is a scattering body throughout, and OpenPBR mixes the diffuse colour towards `subsurface_color` by the weight, so an unset colour (OpenPBR's light grey) would wash the tone out. The shared `Skin_Pores` micro-surface (pores and furrows at a 1 cm tile) is the article's OWN normal and roughness, not a wear overlay: an overlay ships at 0 (C1) and would leave the skin plastic by default. Wear layers at 0 (C1): scratches (overlay 1, damage) and dust/dirt (overlay 2).
name: Skin2_FitzpatrickIV_Clean_Base_s001_v01

sources.note: the skin map (Phase23, pigment, RD-P23-2): CC0 parts only (MPFB2's region masks, hm08, seeded 3D melanin and blood fields through OMF's tabulated two-chromophore model; RD-SKM-2), its average over the skin held to the Physically Based tone below; base_color_const is that tone x the map's peak factor, fuzz_color stays the tone (the average the skin renders)
roughness 0.5 is the MEAN of the Skin_Pores roughness map

sources.why: subsurface_weight 1.0 and subsurface_color = the albedo: skin scatters throughout, and OpenPBR's default subsurface colour (light grey) would desaturate the tone. Phase21 (RD-P21-1, RD-P21-4): the scatter colour now FOLLOWS the base (subsurface_color connected to base_color_out), so it takes the map and the tint; before, it was pinned to the albedo and the tint was inert on skin in every tool (F-P21-3).

Phase22 (RD-P22-17, after click 2: "the shine is still just really over the top"): NO COAT. Phase07 7.3 gave the skin MPFB2's 'enhanced skin' clearcoat (0.1 at roughness 0.3, IOR 1.5) for its oil; on the relief it laid one sharp, wet glint over the whole body, and it double-counted the oil the roughness map's T-zone already carries. The skin's oil and its overall roughness (the map's average, 0.62) are in roughness_map. subsurface_scatter_anisotropy 0.8: tissue scatters strongly forward (a Henyey-Greenstein g of ~0.8 for skin). Fuzz 0.1 in the skin's own albedo, roughness 0.5: fine vellus hair seen at grazing angles, taking roughly the skin's hue (a light grey would put a grey rim on the darker tones); MPFB2 carries no fuzz, so the weight is kept low. Storm ignores the anisotropy (Learnings Storm S8), which adds ~1.2 to the rig's ΔE; Blender is the one honouring it.
